$$h(q) = (0.915)^{3}q$$

The function $h$ is defined by the equation shown. The value of $h(q)$ decreases by $n%$ for each increase by $1$ in the value of $q$. Which of the following is closest to the value of $n$?
explanation: Choice D is correct. When the value of $q$ increases by $1$, the function changes from $h(q) = (0.915)^{3q}$ to $h(q + 1) = (0.915)^{3(q + 1)} = (0.915)^{3q + 3}$. The ratio of the new value to the original value is $\frac{h(q + 1)}{h(q)} = \frac{(0.915)^{3q + 3}}{(0.915)^{3q}} = (0.915)^{3}$, which is approximately $0.766$. Therefore, $h(q + 1)$ is approximately $76.6\%$ of $h(q)$, meaning the value decreases by approximately $100\% - 76.6\% = 23.4\%$ for each increase by $1$ in the value of $q$. Thus, $n$ is approximately $23.4$.
